paragraphs.title: Making the Covenant and Signing by the Leaders

easy.explanation: The people made a written covenant with God.
easy.q: What did the people make with God?

easy.explanation: Nehemiah the Tirshatha is named first among those who sealed it.
easy.q: Who appears first among those who sealed the covenant?

easy.explanation: Zidkijah follows Nehemiah in the opening list.
easy.q: Who is named after Nehemiah?

medium.explanation: The passage says that they sealed and wrote the covenant.
medium.q: What does the written covenant show about the people’s commitment?

medium.explanation: Nehemiah appears first, followed by Zidkijah and then other leaders.
medium.q: Which order is given in the passage?

medium.explanation: Those listed formally confirmed the covenant.
medium.q: What does the word “sealed” mean in this passage?

answers: The commitment was both formal and recorded
challenge.explanation: The covenant was both made officially and written down.
challenge.q: What is shown by the combination of sealing and writing the covenant?

challenge.explanation: His name appears first among those who sealed the covenant.
challenge.q: What does Nehemiah’s place at the beginning of the list indicate?

challenge.explanation: The following verses identify priests, Levites, and leaders of the people.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the broader list of leaders in this section?

short_answers.question: Who was the Tirshatha named in the passage?
short_answers.explanation: Nehemiah is called the Tirshatha.

short_answers.question: Who followed Nehemiah in the opening list?
short_answers.explanation: Zidkijah is named immediately after Nehemiah.

short_answers.question: What did they seal?
short_answers.explanation: They sealed the covenant described in the chapter.

easy.explanation: The section ends by identifying the names as the priests.
easy.q: Which group is listed in this passage?

easy.explanation: The list reads Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah.
easy.q: Which name appears after Azariah?

easy.explanation: The passage says Pashur and Amariah.
easy.q: Who is listed with Pashur?

medium.explanation: The list includes Harim, Meremoth, and Obadiah.
medium.q: Which pair of names appears together in the list?

medium.explanation: The sequence is Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch.
medium.q: Who appears after Daniel?

medium.explanation: The word identifies the group of priestly signers.
medium.q: What does “priests” identify in this passage?

answers: They belong to a list of covenant signers
challenge.explanation: The names are the priests who sealed the covenant.
challenge.q: What do all the names in this section have in common?

challenge.explanation: This is the order at the beginning of the priestly list.
challenge.q: Which sequence is correct?

answers: The names were unrelated to the covenant
challenge.explanation: The numerous names show broad priestly participation.
challenge.q: What does the detailed list suggest?

short_answers.question: Name the first three priests listed.
short_answers.explanation: These are the first three names in the priestly list.

short_answers.question: Who appears after Pashur?
short_answers.explanation: Pashur and Amariah are listed together.

short_answers.question: Which group do these signers belong to?
short_answers.explanation: The passage explicitly identifies them as priests.

easy.explanation: The passage begins its next list with the Levites.
easy.q: Which group signed after the priests?

easy.explanation: Jeshua is called the son of Azaniah.
easy.q: Who is identified as the son of Azaniah?

easy.explanation: Sherebiah is one of the Levites named.
easy.q: Which name appears in the Levite list?

medium.explanation: The passage names Jeshua, Binnui, and Kadmiel together.
medium.q: Who is listed with Binnui and Kadmiel?

medium.explanation: The list includes Micha and Rehob.
medium.q: Which pair appears later in the list?

medium.explanation: The phrase introduces more Levites in the list.
medium.q: What does “their brethren” mean in this context?

challenge.explanation: The chapter first names leaders, then priests, then Levites.
challenge.q: What is the general order of groups so far?

answers: The Levites also accepted responsibility in the covenant
challenge.explanation: Their names appear among those who sealed the covenant.
challenge.q: What does the presence of many Levites suggest?

challenge.explanation: The passage lists Shebaniah, Hodijah, and Kelita in that order.
challenge.q: Which sequence is correct?

short_answers.question: Who was the son of Azaniah?
short_answers.explanation: Jeshua is identified as the son of Azaniah.

short_answers.question: Name two Levites from the passage.
short_answers.answer: Any two of Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Hodijah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan, Micha, Rehob, Hashabiah, Zaccur, Sherebiah, Bani, or Beninu.
short_answers.explanation: These names occur in the Levite list.

short_answers.question: Which group follows the priests?
short_answers.explanation: The Levites are listed after the priests.

paragraphs.title: The Signatures of the People’s Leaders

easy.explanation: The list begins with the chief of the people.
easy.q: Who signed in this section?

easy.explanation: Parosh is the first name in this list.
easy.q: Which name begins the list?

easy.explanation: The passage says Elam, Zatthu, Bani.
easy.q: Who is listed with Zatthu?

medium.explanation: Bebai follows Azgad in the list.
medium.q: Who appears after Azgad?

medium.explanation: The list includes Adonijah and Bigvai together.
medium.q: Which pair appears together?

medium.explanation: The phrase introduces the people’s leaders.
medium.q: What does “the chief of the people” mean?

answers: The participation of many families and leaders
challenge.explanation: Many leaders and families are represented among the signers.
challenge.q: What does the long list of names reflect?

challenge.explanation: The passage lists Ater, Hizkijah, and Azzur.
challenge.q: Which sequence appears correctly?

answers: The signing was organized by leadership groups
The people were unrelated to the covenant
challenge.explanation: The groups are presented in an ordered leadership structure.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from listing the people’s leaders after the priests and Levites?

short_answers.question: Who begins the list of the people’s leaders?
short_answers.explanation: Parosh is the first name in the section.

short_answers.question: Name the three men listed after Ater.
short_answers.answer: Hizkijah and Azzur are listed with Ater.
short_answers.explanation: The sequence is Ater, Hizkijah, Azzur.

short_answers.question: What group is represented in this section?
short_answers.explanation: The passage identifies these signers as the people’s leaders.

paragraphs.title: Accepting the Torah and Social Commitments

answers: The laws of the surrounding nations
easy.explanation: They agreed to walk in God’s law given by Moses.
easy.q: What did the people agree to walk in?

answers: Ware from the people of the land
easy.explanation: They would not buy goods from the people of the land on the sabbath.
easy.q: What would they not buy on the sabbath?

easy.explanation: They agreed to leave the seventh year.
easy.q: Which year would they leave?

answers: By a curse and an oath
medium.explanation: They entered into a curse and an oath.
medium.q: How did the rest of the people enter the covenant?

answers: Not giving daughters to the people of the land or taking their daughters for their sons
Not giving sons to the Levites
medium.explanation: The passage states both parts of the restriction.
medium.q: What did the marriage restriction include?

answers: The collection or enforcement of debts
medium.explanation: It concerns the release from debt obligations in the seventh year.
medium.q: What does “the exaction of every debt” refer to?

answers: God’s law was expressed through practical community rules
God’s law concerned only temple worship
challenge.explanation: The covenant included marriage, Sabbath commerce, and debt obligations.
challenge.q: How are accepting God’s law and the social commitments related?

answers: They would not buy goods from the people of the land
They would not sell anything on weekdays
challenge.explanation: They specifically refused to buy goods on the Sabbath.
challenge.q: What was the practical result of the Sabbath restriction?

answers: They are all commitments of the covenant
They are all names of priests
challenge.explanation: All three appear as obligations accepted by the people.
challenge.q: What do the marriage restriction, Sabbath commerce rule, and seventh year have in common?

short_answers.question: By what two things did the people enter the covenant?
short_answers.answer: By a curse and an oath.
short_answers.explanation: The passage says they entered into a curse and an oath.

short_answers.question: What would they not give to the people of the land?
short_answers.explanation: They would not give their daughters to the people of the land.

short_answers.question: What did they agree to leave?
short_answers.answer: The seventh year and the exaction of every debt.
short_answers.explanation: This is stated in verse 31.

answers: The third part of a shekel
easy.explanation: They pledged the third part of a shekel yearly.
easy.q: How much did the people pledge each year for the house of God?

answers: The service of the house of God
Trade with the people of the land
easy.explanation: The contribution supported the service of God’s house.
easy.q: What was the money for?

easy.explanation: Lots were cast for the wood offering.
easy.q: What was brought to the house of God by lot?

medium.explanation: The passage names shewbread, meat offerings, burnt offerings, and sin offerings.
medium.q: What needs were covered by the yearly contribution?

medium.explanation: All three groups participated in determining the wood offering.
medium.q: Who cast lots for the wood offering?

medium.explanation: Lots were used to determine who would provide the wood.
medium.q: What does “lots” mean in this context?

answers: The contribution supplied needs for worship and sacrifices
challenge.explanation: The money supported offerings and the work of God’s house.
challenge.q: What was the relationship between the contribution and temple service?

answers: They describe different needs of temple worship
challenge.explanation: The passage covers both offerings and wood for the altar.
challenge.q: Why are both sacrifices and wood mentioned?

answers: The commitment was regular and recurring
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates a repeated yearly obligation.
challenge.q: What does “year by year” show?

short_answers.question: How much was pledged each year?
short_answers.answer: The third part of a shekel.
short_answers.explanation: The people charged themselves with this yearly amount.

short_answers.question: For what service was the contribution made?
short_answers.answer: The service of the house of God.
short_answers.explanation: That is the stated purpose of the contribution.

short_answers.question: What offering was chosen by casting lots?
short_answers.explanation: The priests, Levites, and people cast lots for it.

easy.explanation: They promised to bring the firstfruits of their ground and trees.
easy.q: What did the people promise to bring yearly to the house of the LORD?

easy.explanation: The firstborn were brought to the priests who ministered in God’s house.
easy.q: To whom were the firstborn offerings brought?

easy.explanation: The tithes of the ground were given to the Levites.
easy.q: Who received the tithes of the ground?

medium.explanation: The passage names corn, new wine, and oil.
medium.q: Which products are named among the offerings?

answers: The portion the Levites brought to the house of God
The third part of a shekel
medium.explanation: The Levites brought the tithe of the tithes to the treasure house.
medium.q: What was the tithe of the tithes?

answers: The first produce of the harvest
The last produce of the harvest
medium.explanation: Firstfruits are the first produce brought as an offering.
medium.q: What are firstfruits?

challenge.explanation: The passage moves from firstfruits to firstborn offerings and then tithes.
challenge.q: What is the correct order of the commitments in this section?

answers: Each group had a role in receiving and presenting offerings
Only Levites served in the temple
challenge.explanation: Priests received offerings, while Levites received tithes and gave a tenth onward.
challenge.q: What does the distribution among priests and Levites show?

answers: So their offering would also reach the house of God
To sell grain on the Sabbath
challenge.explanation: The Levites brought this portion into the temple treasury.
challenge.q: Why did the Levites bring the tithe of the tithes to the treasure house?

short_answers.question: Who received the tithes of the ground?
short_answers.explanation: The passage assigns the tithes of the ground to the Levites.

short_answers.question: What did the Levites bring to the house of God?
short_answers.explanation: They brought it to the treasure house.

short_answers.question: Name two products brought as offerings.
short_answers.answer: Any two of corn, new wine, oil, firstfruits, or fruit.
short_answers.explanation: These products are named among the offerings.

easy.explanation: The offerings were brought to the chambers of the house of God.
easy.q: Where were the offerings brought?

easy.explanation: The chambers contained the vessels of the sanctuary.
easy.q: What was kept in the chambers?

easy.explanation: The chapter ends with the promise not to forsake God’s house.
easy.q: What did the people promise not to forsake?

medium.explanation: The verse names priests, porters, and singers.
medium.q: Who ministered in the house of God according to the verse?

answers: The chambers received and housed the offerings and sacred vessels
The chambers were used for trade
The chambers were homes for the people
medium.explanation: The offerings were brought to the chambers where the sanctuary vessels were kept.
medium.q: What was the relationship between the chambers and the offerings?

answers: We will not abandon or neglect
medium.explanation: The phrase expresses a promise not to neglect God’s house.
medium.q: What does “we will not forsake” mean?

answers: To support the continuing service of God’s house
challenge.explanation: The offerings supported the vessels and ministers of the house of God.
challenge.q: What was the central purpose of the offerings at the end of the chapter?

answers: It shows that the covenant included ongoing maintenance and worship
It concerns only the names of the signers
challenge.explanation: The final promise ensures that God’s house would not be neglected.
challenge.q: How does the ending connect with the earlier commitments?

answers: Both resources and people were needed for worship
challenge.explanation: The verse mentions the sanctuary vessels and those who served there.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from mentioning both vessels and ministers?

short_answers.question: Where were the offerings brought?
short_answers.answer: To the chambers of the house of God.
short_answers.explanation: The offerings were brought to the temple chambers.

short_answers.question: Name two groups that ministered in the house of God.
short_answers.answer: Any two of the priests, porters, and singers.
short_answers.explanation: These three groups are named in the verse.

short_answers.question: What did the people promise not to forsake?
short_answers.explanation: This is the concluding commitment of the chapter.
